mainEntity.name: Which business tasks are safe to automate first, and which should always stay human-controlled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use AI for research, organization, first drafts, repurposing, and routine checks before assigning it authority to send, publish, spend, or change an account. These lower-risk tasks still need quality review, but they are generally easier to correct than an external action. Context: Run My AI Biz lists recurring research briefs, newsletter drafts, content repurposing, link checks, project updates, billing monitoring, and server-health reporting among possible applications. The suitability of each task depends on data sensitivity, impact, and reversibility. Key factors: - How predictable the inputs are. - Whether mistakes are easy to undo. - Whether another person is affected. - Whether the task requires business judgment. Practical guidance: Start with an internal draft or report, measure correction frequency, and only then consider a controlled execution step. Keep customer communication, spending, sign-ups, and public posting behind explicit approval. Run My AI Biz encourages owners to match automation scope to their actual confidence and capacity.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start with research, organization, first drafts, content repurposing, link checks, and internal reports. Keep sending messages, publishing, spending money, signing up for services, changing accounts, and other hard-to-reverse actions behind explicit approval. Increase scope only after testing and measuring errors.
